answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may influence a shared reputation score. Each bond is locked for a fixed period, and identities caught coordinating false claims lose it; reputation grows only when independent, bonded agents agree over time. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must tie up real capital in many accounts and risks forfeiting it. A shale shipment, a fable, or a mirror account earns no trust merely by multiplying names.
